sources_not_consulted: The DAC FP32, FP16, and INT8 ONNX model files were not downloaded or reprocessed in this review session.
ONNX TensorProto and quantization operator specifications were not independently consulted in this review session.
Cmajor compiler executable, backend code-generation run artifacts, and generated ONNX-to-Cmajor projects were not executed or compiled.
Audio codec numerical-parity, perceptual-quality, and end-to-end runtime measurements were not reproduced.

prompt_premise_corrections.premise: Language-level type support is unverified unless the relevant Cmajor language/compiler artifacts are directly inspected.
prompt_premise_corrections.correction: The condition has now been met for Cmajor release 1.0.3209: its PrimitiveTypeEnum and primitive-type parser directly enumerate the built-in primitive types and contain no INT8 or FLOAT16 primitive. This does not rule out user-defined or packed emulations, which were not verified.

primary_blocker.statement: The reviewed Cmajor 1.0.3209 ONNX emitter maps only FLOAT, DOUBLE, INT64, INT32, and BOOL, while the compiler's built-in PrimitiveTypeEnum and primitive-type parser expose no INT8 or FLOAT16 scalar types and no dedicated ternary type. Supporting these formats therefore requires more than adding an emitter whitelist entry; the representation, compiler type/storage semantics, literal lowering, and relevant operator paths must be designed and validated.

scope_verdict.summary: None of the three formats is near-term in-scope as a native, correctly lowered Cmajor ONNX tensor type in release 1.0.3209. INT8 and FLOAT16 are absent from both the emitter mapping and the inspected built-in primitive type system; ternary has no dedicated ONNX/Cmajor scalar representation in the inspected path. A custom packed or widened representation may be possible, but that is a new design requiring compiler/backend work and codec validation, not existing support.

known.statement: The ONNX emitter's getDataType mapping contains exactly five TensorProto entries: FLOAT→float32, DOUBLE→float64, INT64→int64, INT32→int32, and BOOL→bool; an unlisted data type reaches assert(False).
Cmajor 1.0.3209's PrimitiveTypeEnum enumerates void, int32, int64, float32, float64, boolean, string, complex32, and complex64; it has no int8, float16, or dedicated ternary primitive entry.

The Cmajor primitive-type parser branches for int/int32/int64, float/float32/float64, bool, complex variants, and string; the inspected parser branch contains no int8 or float16 primitive keyword mapping.
Cmajor 1.0.3209's PrimitiveType packed-storage switch assigns 4 bytes to int32 and float32 and 8 bytes to int64 and float64; the switch has no native 1-byte int8 or 2-byte float16 primitive case.

The emitter's generateNode constructs an onnx::operation::<OpType> processor reference from each ONNX node's op_type rather than validating the operator against a complete supported-operator registry at that point; the template's processor declarations determine which names are available to compile.

The shipped Conv processor signature accepts input/output types, kernel-shape values, and dilation values; it does not accept ONNX pads or strides as parameters, and its implementation sets widthPadding to zero.

The checked-in Realm-Quant research note explicitly records that no Cmajor processor was added, no shim was compile-checked, and no WASM was produced in that research effort; these statements are documented in the note and were not independently rerun in this review.

claims.statement: A ternary path could use a custom packed representation with explicit decode/accumulation semantics rather than introducing a scalar ternary primitive, but the packing format, scale metadata, and operator contract have not been designed or measured.

An INT8 path could add native signed/unsigned 8-bit types or use a packed/widened representation, but either approach would need explicit scale and zero-point handling, accumulator rules, and lowering for the actual quantized ONNX operators in the target graph.

A FLOAT16 path could add a native half-precision type or explicitly widen values to an existing type, but storage, literal emission, conversion behavior, arithmetic precision, and target-backend behavior have not been implemented or measured.

A successful emitter extension would require end-to-end tests that compare generated Cmajor execution against a trusted ONNX reference and evaluate codec output quality; source-level type declarations alone would not establish correctness.

type_system.statement: Choose and specify whether INT8 and FLOAT16 are native primitive types or explicitly represented through existing types; define signedness, storage layout, conversions, constants, and arithmetic semantics. Define ternary as a separate packed encoding or explicit scalar abstraction rather than assuming it is an ONNX TensorProto primitive.

emitter_lowering.statement: Extend ONNX datatype handling, tensor/initializer parsing, scalar and array literal serialization, and conversion/lowering paths for each selected representation; reject unsupported combinations with actionable diagnostics rather than an assertion.
Define ternary packing and unpacking at the graph boundary, including how packed weights and any scale/group metadata are represented in generated Cmajor.

operators.statement: Inventory the actual model's quantized operators and implement matching arithmetic, convolution, dequantization, scale/zero-point propagation, and accumulator behavior; do not infer operator coverage from datatype support alone.
Define half-precision conversion and arithmetic lowering, including whether operations execute in half precision or widen to a supported accumulator type.
Define ternary weight decode and accumulation semantics for every operator used by the target graph, including how scale factors are applied.

validation.statement: Add converter fixtures for every supported ONNX tensor datatype, initializer form, constant attribute, and unsupported-type diagnostic; compile generated patches with the pinned Cmajor compiler.

Run operator-level numerical parity tests and end-to-end codec comparisons against a trusted ONNX runtime, including objective and perceptual audio-quality checks; record environment, commands, outputs, and tolerances.

open_design_questions.question: Should ternary weights use fixed 2-bit packing, a wider integer container, or a custom Cmajor aggregate, and where should unpacking occur?
Are scales per-tensor, per-output-channel, per-group, or mixed, and how are zero points represented and propagated?
Which exact ONNX quantized operators and tensor datatypes occur in the target FP16/INT8/ternary graph exports?
Should FLOAT16 be a native compiler scalar type or be widened to FLOAT32 for arithmetic while retaining half-precision storage?
What accumulator precision and rounding/saturation behavior are required for INT8 and ternary convolution and matrix multiplication?
Which compiler backends and deployment targets must support the chosen representation, and what target-specific ABI or code-generation work is required?
Which numerical, codec, and perceptual acceptance thresholds define a successful implementation?

assumptions_and_corrections.statement: The prompt's language-level support status is no longer wholly unverified for Cmajor 1.0.3209: direct inspection of PrimitiveTypeEnum and the primitive parser establishes that native INT8 and FLOAT16 primitive types are absent. This conclusion is release-specific and does not rule out user-defined, packed, or widened emulation.

The scope verdict interprets near-term support as a maintainable native or explicitly supported ONNX-to-Cmajor lowering path, not merely the ability to store quantized bytes inside an arbitrary user-defined aggregate.
Whether a custom aggregate or packed representation can be compiled efficiently by Cmajor backends, and whether it can preserve the target codec's numerical and perceptual behavior, was not verified.

verification_limits: The review used source retrieval only; the Cmajor 1.0.3209 compiler executable was not run and no generated Cmajor patch was compile-checked.
The target DAC ONNX model files were not downloaded or reprocessed in this review session; prior conversion and measurement statements in the research note were not reproduced.
No Cmajor backend code-generation test was run for INT8, FLOAT16, or ternary representations.
No end-to-end codec inference, numerical parity test, audio-quality metric, or perceptual listening evaluation was performed.
The ONNX datatype and quantized-operator specifications were not independently re-read in this review session.
The review schema JSON and review JSON were syntax-parsed, but a dedicated Draft-07 JSON Schema validation engine was not run.
bottom_line: Ternary, INT8, and FLOAT16 are all out of near-term scope as native, validated Cmajor ONNX emitter types in release 1.0.3209.
Direct source inspection confirms that the emitter mapping and Cmajor primitive type system lack the required native representations.
Packed or widened emulation remains a possible research direction, not an implemented or measured capability.
No compiler, codec, or audio-quality validation was performed in this review.
